title: Sunday, Oct. 4 Miami Guide
igCaption:
Sunday, Oct. 4 has a few Miami options with prices attached: complimentary reservations at Superblue, $8 to $15 museum tickets, and a $275 tasting menu in West Palm Beach.
Downtown also has late-night Brightline service after the Kaseya Center event.
Which Sunday plan would you actually do?

Sources: Miami New Times, Eater Miami, Secret Miami

#MiamiEvents #MiamiGuide #MiamiWeekend #SouthFlorida

scenes.text: Sunday, October fourth has Miami plans with real prices attached: complimentary art reservations, museum tickets, and one dinner that costs two hundred seventy-five dollars.

Start at Superblue Miami. James Turrell’s Blue Sea Sky is a room-sized installation made for the immersive art space. Access requires a complimentary on-site reservation, available first-come, first-served.
scenes.caption: Start at Superblue Miami. James Turrell’s Blue Sea Sky is a room-sized installation made for the immersive art space. Access requires a complimentary on-site reservation, available first-come, first-served.

scenes.text: On Miami Beach, the Bass has Yuko Mohri’s Unviolated Imperfection on view through May thirtieth, twenty twenty-seven. It spans three galleries, and tickets cost eight to fifteen dollars.
scenes.caption: On Miami Beach, the Bass has Yuko Mohri’s Unviolated Imperfection on view through May 30, 2027. It spans three galleries, and tickets cost $8 to $15.

scenes.text: Downtown, the Museum of Miami is showing Caught in the Eye: Remembering the nineteen twenty-six Hurricane. It uses photos, newspapers, films, and letters. Tickets cost eight to fifteen dollars.
scenes.caption: Downtown, the Museum of Miami is showing Caught in the Eye: Remembering the 1926 Hurricane. It uses photos, newspapers, films, and letters. Tickets cost $8 to $15.

scenes.text: For dinner, Emelina’s in West Palm Beach has a sixteen-seat Cuban omakase. The ten-course tasting menu costs two hundred seventy-five dollars. The team includes chefs Osmel González and Camila Salazar.
scenes.caption: For dinner, Emelina’s in West Palm Beach has a 16-seat Cuban omakase. The 10-course tasting menu costs $275. The team includes chefs Osmel González and Camila Salazar.

scenes.text: If your Sunday ends near Kaseya Center, Brightline has late-night trains from MiamiCentral after the Don Omar concert. The station sits less than a mile from the arena, about a fifteen-minute walk.
scenes.caption: If your Sunday ends near Kaseya Center, Brightline has late-night trains from MiamiCentral after the Don Omar concert. The station sits less than a mile from the arena, about a 15-minute walk.

scenes.text: Pick your first Sunday stop. A good Sunday in Miami is partly about where you go, and partly about the people moving through the same places, which is the quiet idea behind NEAR.
